title: Normalized supported pro-etale realization of an integral extension
statement: Fix the finite datum $P$ of [def-pur-conventions], a $k$-scheme $T$ and a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. For an integral extension $\beta$, let $b_A(\beta)$ be [def-pur-framed-scalar-realization]. Define $b_A^{\mathrm{pro}}(\beta)$ to be the unique element satisfying the normalized support-Hom comparison predicate [def-pur-framed-pro-predicate] for $b_A(\beta)$. Existence and uniqueness are part of this characterization; its support cohomology group, cocycle normalization, canonical site comparison and roots coefficient are exactly those of the predicate. No arbitrary comparison or trivialization is selected.

source.place: Stacks 03AJ torsors-h1; 03PL Kummer sequence; 0A45 support triangle. Framed-line construction in blueprint main-20261015 lem-pur-divisor-class.proof.md, first sentence and final paragraph.

proof.text: Use the normalized pro-etale supported-Hom identification supplied by [lem-pur-supported-hom-pullback]. Its additive equivalence identifies the actual right-derived supported group in degree two with the shifted Hom group in the predicate. No compatibility with another site map is needed to invert this equivalence.

Any two normalized identifications agree. On a degreewise injective bounded-below complex, lift the supported class through the canonical supportSequenceModelIso and the surjective homology projection to a supported cocycle. Apply the evaluation and cocycle clauses of [lem-pur-supported-hom-cocycle-normalization] to obtain its representing map from the ordinary supported constant. Precompose with the canonical isomorphism from the etale-origin supported constant; its composite with the actual constant restriction is the ordinary restriction. Both Identification.normalization clauses therefore give the identical localized map. For a general bounded-below derived object choose a degreewise injective representative. Naturality identifies both comparisons after the same invertible shifted map; cancel that map.

Let b be the canonical site-comparison Hom image already specified by [def-pur-framed-pro-predicate], applied to the scalar realization. Invert the chosen normalized supported-Hom equivalence on b. Step 2 makes the image of this class equal b for every normalized identification, proving the predicate. Conversely the predicate evaluated at the chosen identification and injectivity of that equivalence prove uniqueness. This argument applies to every scalar Ext class, and hence to every integral extension in the statement.

proof_origin.place: Section 9, Theorem 9.4, Example 9.5 and injective-resolution Ext proof, pp. 66–67; Q7 inverse-equivalence assembly and normalization uniqueness, 2026-10-25.
